audit.title: Agent Work Accountability skill audit
audit.scope_rule: Count canonical skill directories under skills/. Treat installation symlinks as aliases, not duplicate skills.
audit.usage_rule: Count a use once per distinct session when the session reads SKILL.md or the user invokes the skill by name or slash command. Repeated reads in one session are de-duplicated.

tier_rule.Core: 4 or more distinct sessions in 30 days (weekly or more)
tier_rule.Dormant: No verified use only when every relevant history source is readable
tier_rule.No data: At least one required history source is unreadable or uninspected

source_state.note: The audit evaluated the final remediated tree before publication; reports/ is excluded so this digest remains stable when the artifacts are committed.
source_state.digest_scope: All tracked and untracked repository files except reports/ and Git-ignored files, hashed by sorted path and content.

coverage.note: JSONL session roots searched; repeated reads within a session were de-duplicated.
Project JSONL sessions searched; tool-result wrappers were not counted as separate uses.

Historical SQLite usage remains No data because the 12 GB database was not inspected. Live Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3 review sessions and a skill-tool discovery smoke were directly observed; they are excluded from the pre-audit usage tier.

skills.name: github-work-accountability
skills.purpose: Turn ADRs, PRDs, and design proposals into source-bound GitHub epics and stories, then keep phase, priority, blockers, evidence, and delivery state accurate.
triggers: A planning document must become GitHub work
A repository or Project needs the accountability schema
An ADR or other planning source changed
Execution, acceptance, release, blocker, or priority facts changed
Existing issues must be reconciled with source and Git evidence
inputs: Repository instructions and native planning-source policy
Canonical planning source, lifecycle/status, Git commit, blob, and quoted anchors
GitHub owner, actor, issues, Project, fields, labels, relationships, and capabilities
Proposed extraction manifest with stable work keys and dependency graph
Bound implementation, acceptance, evidence, and release facts
Optional live observations from an external agent-communication adapter
outputs: Source-bound GitHub epic and story issues with durable work keys
Capability-appropriate Project fields, views, or repository labels
Phase, health, source freshness, priority, rank, and dependency state
Acceptance and release evidence without loss of issue history
Idempotent reconciliation of changed planning sources
Deterministic ADR inspection and extraction-validation reports

relationship_summary.note: The in-scope skill names no other skill. Its Markdown links resolve to bundled references. Only verified installation-alias edges are shown.

overlaps.overlap: Name and broad GitHub project-management trigger territory.
overlaps.difference: The comparator is a generated placeholder with no usable trigger or workflow; the audited skill defines a complete source-to-delivery protocol.
overlaps.recommendation: Retire or quarantine the placeholder to remove trigger ambiguity.

overlaps.overlap: Both may read or mutate GitHub issues.
overlaps.difference: GitHub Automation covers repository hosting actions, PRs, CI, and releases; it does not define planning decomposition, source binding, or lifecycle truth.
overlaps.recommendation: Keep separate; document a handoff only after both skills name the boundary explicitly.

overlaps.overlap: Both inspect ADR content and repository-native policy.
overlaps.difference: The r2c skills own one repository's ADR schema and lifecycle; the audited skill consumes any repository's planning source and owns GitHub accountability.
overlaps.recommendation: Keep separate; add an explicit reconciliation handoff in the repository adapter.

overlaps.overlap: Both can be triggered by ADR creation, review, or indexing work.
overlaps.difference: The Ruflo family owns ADR lifecycle and AgentDB-oriented operations; the audited skill intentionally treats ADR managers and memory as optional adapters.
overlaps.recommendation: Keep separate and do not merge lifecycle assumptions into the portable skill.

recommendations.subject: github-work-accountability
recommendations.reason: One coherent accountability boundary, verified discovery in all three clients, and no substantiated P0/P1 after remediation.
recommendations.action: Commit and publish the reviewed fixes, then continue the ADR-059 pilot.

recommendations.subject: Repository adoption interlock
recommendations.reason: A portable skill cannot force unrelated ADR or plan writers to reconcile linked GitHub work.
recommendations.action: Add a repository-local check/adapter that fails closed when a linked planning blob changes without reconciliation.

recommendations.subject: Installer lifecycle edges
recommendations.reason: Branch updates are proved, but tag/SHA updates and removed-skill cleanup are not.
recommendations.action: Specify ref semantics and add provenance-backed stale-link cleanup before a second skill ships.

recommendations.subject: r2c/github-project-management placeholder
recommendations.reason: Its generic name overlaps this skill while its file contains placeholder trigger text.
recommendations.action: Remove it from discovery or replace it with an explicit redirect after checking its history.

recommendations.subject: Usage observability
recommendations.reason: Historical OpenCode usage is No data and raw histories require client-specific parsing.
recommendations.action: Define an optional client-neutral usage receipt before the next library-wide audit.

brand_gaps.finding: The repository is branded as a skill pack while it contains one canonical skill.

post_audit_activity.reason: Audit and review activity would otherwise manufacture its own usage signal.
post_audit_activity.observed: Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, Fable, and explicit OpenCode/Claude discovery smokes received or loaded the skill after the cutoff.

rejected_or_conditional: The claimed piped cwd-adoption defect was disproved on the original script, then became reproducible after main() wrapping and was fixed with an actual-file guard.
The post-fix gh_account omission was conditional and false: the helper is tracked at the base commit.
The post-fix Bash 3.2 no-target claim was disproved by exit 2 with the actionable no-target message and added as a regression test.
independent_reviews.post_fix: No substantiated P0-P2 remained in the reviewed diff; one future stale-symlink cleanup gap remains from the initial review.
The post-fix request returned no report; remediation is supported by local regression tests rather than inferred reviewer approval.

independent_reviews.initial_verdict: FAIL until installer blocker fixed; PASS WITH FIXES afterward
independent_reviews.post_fix: The focused post-fix request timed out without a report; the original findings were remediated and covered locally.

remediations: Made Bash array expansion safe on stock macOS Bash 3.2 and wrapped execution in main() so truncated pipes cannot partially run.
Made unchanged --copy installs idempotent, excluded generated cache files, made mode changes explicit, preflighted all conflicts, and uniquified backups.
Tested piped managed clone, fast-forward update, dirty-checkout refusal, neutral working directory, path spaces, preset whitespace, and link/copy transitions.
Required repository-qualified keys, validation methods, delivery boundaries, and per-story coverage in extraction-v1.
Replaced search-index absence checks with paginated Issues API enumeration, PR exclusion, exact marker matching, and post-create re-enumeration.
Specified client-neutral pending-operation identity, storage, replay, and stale-source behavior.
Fixed ADR working-tree hashing with Git filters and preserved underscores and lower-level headings.
Added isolated gh account-helper tests and made Python 3 requirements explicit.

remaining_risks.finding: A skill removed from a future multi-skill pack can leave a dangling installed symlink.
remaining_risks.action: Add installer provenance and safe stale-link cleanup before shipping a second skill.

remaining_risks.finding: WORK_ACCOUNTABILITY_REF update semantics are proven for branches but not tags or raw commit IDs.
remaining_risks.action: Either constrain and document the variable as a branch name or implement detached tag/SHA updates with tests.

remaining_risks.finding: Installing the skill cannot force unrelated planning-document writers to reconcile GitHub.
remaining_risks.action: Build the separate repository adoption interlock/check before relying on freshness as an enforced invariant.
